source_text: Non timuisti, scelestissime, hoc applicare Deo, quod ne ei admoveret Manichaeus, commentus est alium conditorem; ambo quidem estis veritatis inimici, sed putabatur ante te non posse ille impietate superari.
pass_a_gloss: You did not fear, most criminal, to apply this to God, which lest the Manichaean move it to him, he invented another founder; both indeed you are enemies of the truth, but it was thought before you that he could not be surpassed in impiety.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: You did not fear, most wicked man, to apply to God something for which the Manichaean invented another creator precisely to avoid attributing it to him. Both of you are enemies of the truth, but before you it was thought impossible to surpass him in impiety.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
LS pietas: duty to God/kin. Julian pairs it with ratio as catholic fortification.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
